remediation_steps.step:
Back up the current Terraform file to ensure changes can be reverted if necessary.

Command:
    cp /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab/main.tf /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab/main.tf.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)

Why: Backing up the file allows for easy rollback in case the changes need to be undone.

Update the IAM policy to remove overly permissive actions and implement least privilege.

Command:
    sed -i 's/Action   = "s3:ListBucket"/Action   = "s3:GetObject"/' /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab/main.tf

Why: Restricting the IAM policy to specific actions reduces the risk of unauthorized data access.

Plan the Terraform changes to ensure the updated policy is correctly configured.

Command:
    cd /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab && terraform plan -detailed-exitcode

Why: Planning the changes allows for verification of the intended updates before applying them.

Apply the Terraform changes to update the IAM policy in the AWS environment.

Command:
    terraform apply -auto-approve

Why: Applying the changes updates the IAM policy to enforce the principle of least privilege.

Verify the IAM policy changes using Checkov to ensure the vulnerability is resolved.

Command:
    checkov -d /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab --check CKV_AWS_288 --output json --quiet --compact

Why: Re-scanning with Checkov confirms that the policy no longer violates security best practices.

Review the IAM policy to ensure no other overly permissive actions remain.

Command:
    grep 'Action' /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab/main.tf

Why: Ensuring no other overly permissive actions remain helps maintain a secure IAM policy.
